editorial.headline: A Living Institution for Conservation, Learning and Recreation
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the operators of botanical gardens, zoos and aquariums—open to full foreign ownership nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This is an operational activity: it covers the day-to-day running of botanical gardens and zoos, including those where children interact directly with animals, together with aquariums. Its centre of gravity reaches further into conservation: ex situ areas for breeding or rescuing plants and animals outside their natural habitat, while preserving the integrity of their species. These institutions are used for education, display, research, scientific development and recreation. The scope embraces wildlife parks and specialised animal parks, specialist animal training centres, botanical gardens, herbaria, zoological museums and specialist plant gardens. It is the operation of a public-interest conservation institution, not simply an attraction.

The code is open to operators at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. It therefore accommodates institutions across all four stated business scales. The registrant is the operator: the party running a garden, zoo, aquarium, animal park, herbarium or other named conservation institution. Across those settings, the common thread is a managed place where plants or animals are conserved, displayed and used for learning, research and recreation.

Nationally, the investment position is direct. The record classifies the activity as TERBUKA, with PMA maximum foreign ownership of 100%. Foreign capital may therefore own the activity in full at the national level. This is the ceiling stated by the record, supported by Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In this activity’s own terms, both the operational scope and national ownership position are explicit.

The Bali picture is also clear, but it must be read through the provincial moratorium. Bali permanently blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI across the island. This activity is nevertheless recorded as not blocked. The stated reason is that, at Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi; its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. For PMA registration, this activity remains open in Bali and is not a moratorium exclusion. That conclusion follows precisely from the Bali record supplied.
